Meir Fenigstein: One Man’s Show

JEWISH JOURNAL · BY AYALA OR-EL · FEB 11, 2026

← ALL COVERAGE
Meir Fenigstein at the opening night gala of the 36th Israel Film Festival, Saban Theatre, Nov 13, 2024. Photo: Michael Tullberg / Getty Images
PUBLISHED INJewish JournalBy Ayala Or-El · Feb 11, 2026 · 17 min read
SHARE
FacebookWhatsAppEmail

How Meir Fenigstein brings Israeli stories to the American screen.

[Sample summary — replace with the licensed article text.] At 75, the festival’s founder still runs it almost single-handedly: curating, fundraising, promoting and presenting Israeli films to American audiences, flying in from Tel Aviv several times a year.

The profile traces his path from drummer in Kaveret, one of Israel’s most beloved bands, to a music student in Boston who was asked to bring two Israeli films to campus, and ended up launching a festival instead.

“I see this as a mission for the State of Israel.”— Meir Fenigstein

From a sold-out first weekend in Boston, to a freezing opening night in New York, to Los Angeles in 1986, the article follows how the festival grew, and the people who helped it along the way.

Today the festival takes place in Los Angeles only, and still opens each year at the Saban Theatre, with filmmakers flying in from Israel to meet their audiences.

Originally published in Jewish Journal READ THE FULL ARTICLE ↗

Become a
Volunteer

Join the team behind the biggest platform for Israeli films in the U.S.

APPLY NOW
38TH ISRAEL FILM FESTIVAL · NOV 18–24, 2026

Be part of the biggest platform for Israeli films in the U.S.

We're looking for enthusiastic, dedicated volunteers to help at our screenings and special events at the Writers Guild Theater, Saban Theater and Fine Arts Theatre in Beverly Hills, and Laemmle Town Center 5 in Encino, as we showcase over 30 of the newest and most exciting films from Israel.

Thank you for wanting to donate your time and talent. Fill out the form, share it with friends who might want to join, and see you at the movies!

How you'll help

  • Screenings & events welcoming audiences and guests at the theatres.
  • Ticketing before and during the festival.
  • Promotion spreading the word and distributing flyers around the city.

What you'll get

  • New friends from a community that loves Israeli film.
  • Industry access meet filmmakers, actors and industry leaders.
  • The films watch the newest Israeli cinema.
Ready to join us? Questions? Email coordinator@israelfilmfestival.org

Our Mission
& History

Founded in 1982 with six films and a dream, today the largest showcase for Israeli film in the United States.

GALLERY & ARCHIVE →GALLERY

Six films and a dream.

Founded by Meir Fenigstein in 1982, the Israel Film Festival has grown to become one of the most important Israeli cultural events in the world, and the largest showcase for Israeli films in the United States.

For over four decades it has spotlighted Israel's thriving film and television industry, offering an intercultural exchange that advances tolerance and understanding, and enriches the American vision of Israel's social and cultural diversity.

Presented annually by IsraFest Foundation, Inc., a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Los Angeles.

{{ st.n }}{{ st.l }}
OUR MISSION

To brand Israel as the lively and innovative nation that it is, shining a spotlight on its thriving film and television industry and enriching the American experience of Israel's social and cultural diversity.

As an international entertainment industry event, the festival has brought acclaim to the films and their makers, and opened new possibilities for cooperation and co-production between the U.S. and Israeli film and TV industries. Each year it premieres Israeli features, documentaries, television dramas and student shorts, alongside conversations with visiting Israeli filmmakers.

FOUNDER & EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR

Meir Fenigstein

Once known as Poogy, the drummer of the legendary Israeli rock band Kaveret, he channeled that energy into a love of Israeli cinema.

Founder and Executive Director of IsraFest Foundation, Inc. and the Israel Film Festival in the USA, Meir has spent four decades raising awareness of Israel's cultural diversity and cinematic creativity. He has earned industry respect for elevating Israeli film and television in America, and for building an artistic bridge that fosters understanding between Israel, the U.S. and the world.
